events.title: Endeavour Strikes the Great Barrier Reef
events.description: Captain James Cook's ship HMS Endeavour ran onto a coral reef off the coast of present-day Queensland, Australia. The crew lightened the ship and managed to float it free. They then made repairs on shore at the site of modern Cooktown.
events.significance: The near-disaster was a defining moment of Cook's first Pacific voyage. It also gave Europeans an early, hard-won lesson about the dangers of navigating the world's largest coral reef system.

events.title: First Public Demonstration of FM Radio
events.description: Inventor Edwin Armstrong gave the first public demonstration of FM broadcasting in the United States, at Alpine, New Jersey.
events.significance: Frequency modulation delivered clearer, static-free sound than AM radio. It went on to shape music broadcasting and modern wireless communication.

events.title: Escape from Alcatraz
events.description: Frank Morris and brothers John and Clarence Anglin slipped out of their cells at the island prison in San Francisco Bay. They left dummy heads in their beds and set off on a homemade raft.
events.significance: It is the only escape from Alcatraz that has never been conclusively explained. The men were never found, and the case has inspired books, films and decades of debate. The prison closed in 1963.

events.title: Stand in the Schoolhouse Door
events.description: Alabama Governor George Wallace stepped aside after defiantly blocking the entrance to an auditorium at the University of Alabama. His move allowed two Black students to enroll.
events.significance: The confrontation was a landmark in the struggle over school desegregation. That evening President John F. Kennedy gave his national address on civil rights.
